simple.meaning: סָעִף (çâʻiph) is a Hebrew word meaning “divided (in mind), i.e. (abstractly) a sentiment.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: סָעִף (H5587) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 18:21, with occurrences in 1 Kings, Job.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סָעִף (H5587) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in סָעִף (H5587) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: סָעִף (çâʻiph) / H5587 is traced through 1 Kings 18:21, Job 4:13, Job 20:2 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H5587. saiph [ סְעִמָּה ] noun feminine division, divided opinion ; — plural absolute הַסְּעִמִּים עַלשְֿׁתֵּי 1Kin 18:21 how long are ye limping on the two divided opinions (as on unequal legs; ᵐ5 ταῖς ἰγνύαις seems an attempt to interpret the figurative; according to Albr ZAW xvi (1896) 75 {abbrev } ס really = legs ). שְׂעִמִּים noun [masculine] plural disquietings , = disquieting or excited thoughts; — ׳שׂ Job 4:13 ; suffix שְׂעִמַּי (Baer שְׂעִימַּי ) 20:2 (|| חוּשִׁי ).

occurrences.englishText: Elijah came near to all the people, and said, “How long will you waver between the two sides? If Yahweh is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.”
